groups.title: ア row

chars.mnemonic: A sharp antenna bent by the wind: "a". Katakana are angular where hiragana are curvy.
A person leaning on a stick: "ee". Two straight strokes.
A roof with a chimney: "u". It is ワ with a hat; hiragana う has the same top.
An elevator door frame, a capital I on its side: "e" for エレベーター.
A figure carrying a pole over the shoulder: "oh!"
A dash that stretches the vowel before it for one extra beat: コーヒー is ko-o-hi-i. Vertical text turns it vertical.

groups.note: Katakana writes the same 46 sounds as hiragana with angular strokes. It is used for loanwords (コーヒー), foreign names, animal and plant names in science, onomatopoeia, and emphasis. The long-vowel mark ー replaces the extra vowel kana hiragana uses: hiragana おかあさん, katakana カー.

groups.title: カ row

chars.mnemonic: Hiragana か without its dash: the same karate kick.
A key with two teeth: き without the bottom loop.
A cuckoo's open beak: "ku". Watch out for タ (ク with a dot inside).
A capital K leaning back: "ke".
The corner of a box: "ko" for corner.

groups.note: Loanword rule 1: English consonant clusters get a vowel inserted, usually u (ク, ス, ト takes o): "cake" → ケーキ, "ice" → アイス.

groups.title: サ row

chars.mnemonic: The top of さ, straightened: a samurai's crossguard with the sword below.
Three drops sliding in from the left, with a smile swept upward: "she" smiles. Compare ツ, whose drops fall from above.
A skier gliding downhill: "su" for スキー.
Hiragana せ with straight lines: a set of bars.
Two drops falling from above: "so". Compare ン, which has one drop and a flatter sweep.

groups.note: Loanword rule 2: a long English vowel or an -er/-or ending becomes ー: "course" → コース, "soccer" → サッカー. シ (drops from the side) and ツ (drops from above) are the most-confused pair; so are ソ and ン.

groups.title: タ row

chars.mnemonic: ク with a dot inside: a taco shell with filling.
A capital T with a flag on top: a cheerleader waving.
A tsunami: two drops falling from above and a wave sweeping up. Compare シ, whose drops come from the side.
A telephone pole with two crossbars.
A boot seen from the side with a toe sticking out: "to".

groups.note: ツ and シ: in ツ the two short strokes point down and the sweep rises steeply; in シ the short strokes point right and the sweep is flatter. Note スーツ (suit) and スカート (skirt): "t" before a vowel-less ending becomes ト.

groups.title: ナ row

chars.mnemonic: A knife blade with a crossguard: "na" for ナイフ.
Two lines: ni is "two" (二) in Japanese.
Noodles draped over chopsticks: "nu".
A cat (neko) sitting on a stake, tail hanging down.
A single stroke: a nose in profile, "no".

groups.note: ナ (two strokes, straight) versus メ (two strokes, crossing low). Words you already know in hiragana (いぬ, ねこ) stay hiragana; katakana is for words that came from other languages.

groups.title: ハ row

chars.mnemonic: Two sides of a wide-open laughing mouth: "ha ha".
A heel seen from the side: "hee".
A hood pulled over the top of Mount Fuji: "fu". Compare ワ (closed on the left) and ウ (with a hat).
Identical to hiragana へ: a small heap.
A holy cross with two drops: "ho".

groups.note: フ, ワ and ウ share a family: フ is open on the left, ワ is closed, ウ wears a hat. コーヒー (coffee) is the classic four-beat word: ko-o-hi-i.

groups.title: マ row

chars.mnemonic: A 7 with a tail: a magnet pulling to the right, "ma".
Three lines: mi is "three" (三) in Japanese.
A cow's muzzle with a tuft: "moo".
A needle crossing a thread: "me" marks the spot. Compare ナ (straight bar).
Hiragana も without its bottom hook: more bars.

groups.note: Loanword rule 3: English "-er" at the end becomes aa with ー: "maker" → メーカー, "motor" → モーター. ム looks like a cow's nose; マ is a 7 with a tail.

groups.title: ヤ row

chars.mnemonic: Hiragana や without the loop: a yak's horn.
A U-turn sign laid flat: "yu".
A mirrored capital E: three shelves for your yoghurt.

groups.note: Small ャ, ュ, ョ are introduced in the combinations group. The full-size ヤ ユ ヨ you learn here are their own beats.

groups.title: ラ row

chars.mnemonic: A ramen bowl with its lid lifted: "ra".
Hiragana り with the strokes separated: two reeds.
A root splitting in two: "ru". Compare レ (one stroke).
A lever, or a leg kicking: "re".
A square mouth, a robot's mouth: "ro".

groups.note: The r-row is the busiest in loanwords because English l and r both become the Japanese r: "rule" → ルール, "lace" and "race" are both レース. ル (two strokes) versus レ (one stroke).

groups.title: ワ・ヲ・ン

chars.mnemonic: A wide box with a lid: "wa". ウ is ワ with a hat; フ is ワ without the left side.
ラ with an extra bar. Rare: it appears only in old texts and stylised writing. Pronounced "o".
One drop from above and a long upward sweep: "n". Compare ソ (two drops, steeper sweep).

groups.note: ン closes a syllable: パン, レストラン. It is one beat on its own. ソ versus ン: ソ's sweep starts from the top; ン's sweep starts low and rises.

groups.title: ガ row (dakuten)
groups.intro: Two small dots (゛) at the top right turn k into g, exactly as in hiragana.

chars.mnemonic: カ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ga. Same shape, voiced sound.
キ with two dots (dakuten) becomes gi. Same shape, voiced sound.
ク with two dots (dakuten) becomes gu. Same shape, voiced sound.
ケ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ge. Same shape, voiced sound.
コ with two dots (dakuten) becomes go. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: Voiced consonants work exactly as in hiragana. English "-ing" becomes イング: ハイキング, ショッピング.

groups.title: ザ row (dakuten)
groups.intro: The dakuten turns s into z. ジ is "ji".

chars.mnemonic: サ with two dots (dakuten) becomes za. Same shape, voiced sound.
シ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ji. Same shape, voiced sound.
ス with two dots (dakuten) becomes zu. Same shape, voiced sound.
セ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ze. Same shape, voiced sound.
ソ with two dots (dakuten) becomes zo. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: ジ is "ji": ジム (gym), ラジオ (radio). English "z" and "th" both tend to become ザ-row sounds.

groups.title: ダ row (dakuten)
groups.intro: The dakuten turns t into d. ヂ and ヅ are very rare.

chars.mnemonic: タ with two dots (dakuten) becomes da. Same shape, voiced sound.
チ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ji. Same shape, voiced sound.
ツ with two dots (dakuten) becomes zu. Same shape, voiced sound.
テ with two dots (dakuten) becomes de. Same shape, voiced sound.
ト with two dots (dakuten) becomes do. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: English "d" + vowel is straightforward; a bare "d" at the end becomes ド: カード (card), ガイド (guide).

groups.title: バ row (dakuten)
groups.intro: The dakuten turns h into b.

chars.mnemonic: ハ with two dots (dakuten) becomes ba. Same shape, voiced sound.
ヒ with two dots (dakuten) becomes bi. Same shape, voiced sound.
フ with two dots (dakuten) becomes bu. Same shape, voiced sound.
ヘ with two dots (dakuten) becomes be. Same shape, voiced sound.
ホ with two dots (dakuten) becomes bo. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: English "v" is usually written with the バ row: テレビ (television), ビル (building). ヴ exists for precision but is optional.

groups.title: パ row (handakuten)
groups.intro: The small circle (゜) turns h into p.

chars.mnemonic: ハ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pa. Same shape, voiced sound.
ヒ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pi. Same shape, voiced sound.
フ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pu. Same shape, voiced sound.
ヘ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes pe. Same shape, voiced sound.
ホ with a small circle (handakuten) becomes po. Same shape, voiced sound.

groups.note: Half-voiced p sounds carry a lot of everyday vocabulary: パン, ペン, パソコン (pasokon, from "personal computer").

groups.title: Combinations (キャ, シュ, チョ…)
groups.intro: Combine an i-row katakana with a small ャ, ュ or ョ. The two symbols make one beat.

chars.mnemonic: キ (ki) + small ャ = kya, said as one beat.
キ (ki) + small ュ = kyu, said as one beat.
キ (ki) + small ョ = kyo, said as one beat.
シ (shi) + small ャ = sha, said as one beat.
シ (shi) + small ュ = shu, said as one beat.
シ (shi) + small ョ = sho, said as one beat.
チ (chi) + small ャ = cha, said as one beat.
チ (chi) + small ュ = chu, said as one beat.
チ (chi) + small ョ = cho, said as one beat.
ニ (ni) + small ャ = nya, said as one beat.
ニ (ni) + small ュ = nyu, said as one beat.
ニ (ni) + small ョ = nyo, said as one beat.
ヒ (hi) + small ャ = hya, said as one beat.
ヒ (hi) + small ュ = hyu, said as one beat.
ヒ (hi) + small ョ = hyo, said as one beat.
ミ (mi) + small ャ = mya, said as one beat.
ミ (mi) + small ュ = myu, said as one beat.
ミ (mi) + small ョ = myo, said as one beat.
リ (ri) + small ャ = rya, said as one beat.
リ (ri) + small ュ = ryu, said as one beat.
リ (ri) + small ョ = ryo, said as one beat.

groups.note: Small ャ ュ ョ blend into one beat, as in hiragana. English "sh", "ch", "ny" and "-ure" endings land here: シャツ, チャンス, ニュース, ミュージック.

groups.title: Voiced combinations (ギャ, ジュ, ビョ…)
groups.intro: The same pattern with dakuten and handakuten katakana.

chars.mnemonic: ギ (gi) + small ャ = gya, said as one beat.
ギ (gi) + small ュ = gyu, said as one beat.
ギ (gi) + small ョ = gyo, said as one beat.
ジ (ji) + small ャ = ja, said as one beat.
ジ (ji) + small ュ = ju, said as one beat.
ジ (ji) + small ョ = jo, said as one beat.
ビ (bi) + small ャ = bya, said as one beat.
ビ (bi) + small ュ = byu, said as one beat.
ビ (bi) + small ョ = byo, said as one beat.
ピ (pi) + small ャ = pya, said as one beat.
ピ (pi) + small ュ = pyu, said as one beat.
ピ (pi) + small ョ = pyo, said as one beat.

groups.note: Voiced combinations: ジャ ジュ ジョ carry English "j" and soft "g": ジャム, ジュース, ジョギング.

groups.title: Small ッ (double consonants)
groups.intro: Small ッ marks a doubled consonant: the sound stops for one beat.

chars.mnemonic: A small ツ. Not pronounced: it doubles the next consonant with a one-beat pause, as in ベッド (bed).

groups.note: Small ッ doubles the next consonant and often appears where English has a short, clipped vowel: bed → ベッド, cup → カップ, net → ネット.

groups.title: Extended combinations (ファ, ティ, ウェ…)
groups.intro: Katakana borrows sounds Japanese never had by pairing a kana with a small vowel: ファ, ティ, ウェ, ヴァ.

chars.mnemonic: フ + small ァ: fa, as in ファン (fan).
フ + small ィ: fi, as in フィルム (film).
フ + small ェ: fe, as in カフェ (café).
フ + small ォ: fo, as in フォーク (fork).
テ + small ィ: a true "ti" sound, as in ティー (tea). Compare チ (chi).
デ + small ィ: "di", as in ディナー (dinner).
ウ + small ィ: "wi", as in ウィンドウ (window).
ウ + small ェ: "we", as in ウェブ (web).
ウ + small ォ: "wo", as in ウォーター (water).
シ + small ェ: "she", as in シェフ (chef).
ジ + small ェ: "je", as in ジェット (jet).
チ + small ェ: "che", as in チェック (check).
ヴ (ウ with dakuten) + small ァ: "va". Many people say and write バ instead.
デ + small ュ: "dyu", as in プロデューサー (producer).
ト + small ゥ: a true "tu", as in タトゥー (tattoo).

groups.note: Extended combinations use small ァ ィ ゥ ェ ォ to reach sounds Japanese did not have: ファ (fa), ティ (ti), ウェ (we), ヴァ (va). They appear only in loanwords and names. Usage varies: ヴァイオリン and バイオリン are both common.
